title: Justice Department Files to Intervene and Dismiss Lawsuit that Would Hamper America’s AI Innovation and Security

reading.body:
The summary filed with this incident is not a summary. It is a message from a language model saying that it could not read the document it was given, that the file appeared corrupted, and that the user should re-upload it or paste the text. The text addresses a reader directly and offers numbered options. It was nonetheless recorded as the account of the incident.

The failure sits at the join between document ingestion and summarisation. A PDF did not parse into readable text, and the unreadable input was passed onward to a model that was asked to summarise it. The model returned a message about the input rather than a summary of it, and nothing downstream checked that the output described the source. Catching this would have taken two checks that are cheap to run: a validation that the document parsed into text before it is summarised, and a validation that the returned text is a summary of that document rather than a remark about it. A human reading the record before publication would also have caught it.

The report titles name a power project, a data centre, a notice of intent to sue under the Clean Air Act, a complaint and a Justice Department filing. None of that is described in the summary, so nothing about those events is established here. A notice of intent to sue is not a finding, a complaint is not a verdict, and a filing is not a ruling. It is also not established which system produced the text, or why the document failed to parse.

I apologize, but the document you've provided appears to be a corrupted or improperly formatted PDF file. The text content is largely unreadable, consisting mainly of encoding artifacts, binary data, and garbled characters rather than coherent article text.

To provide you with an accurate two-paragraph summary as requested, I would need a readable version of the article. Please try one of the following:

1. Re-upload the document in a cleaner format
2. Copy and paste the article text directly
3. Provide the original URL or source

Once you provide readable source material, I'll be happy to create a concise 120-180 word summary in plain language covering what happened, who is involved, key numbers, and next steps.
